learningObjectives: Plan a basic usability test around a specific user goal.
Identify usability problems from user behavior and feedback.
Distinguish observations from assumptions when evaluating usability.
Prioritize findings based on their impact on task completion.

activities.title: Usability Test Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages of a basic usability test.

content.concept: Usability testing involves defining goals, preparing tasks, recruiting participants, observing behavior, collecting findings, and synthesizing results.
content.tip: Start with the research goal and finish by turning observations into findings.

activities.title: Test Task Builder
activities.instruction: Build a clear and realistic usability test task.

content.concept: A good usability task gives users a realistic goal without unnecessarily revealing the exact steps they should take.
content.tip: Focus on what the user wants to accomplish rather than telling them how to accomplish it.

activities.title: Usability Problem Detector
activities.instruction: Identify the usability issue demonstrated in each scenario.

content.concept: Usability problems can appear as confusion, errors, hesitation, inefficient paths, repeated actions, or inability to complete a task.
content.tip: Focus on observable user behavior rather than guessing the user's thoughts.

choices: User cannot find the primary action
User successfully recovers from an error
config.answer: User cannot find the primary action

activities.title: Finding Priority Lab
activities.instruction: Adjust severity and frequency to understand finding priority.

content.concept: Usability findings can be prioritized using factors such as severity, frequency, and impact on important user tasks.
content.tip: A frequent problem that prevents users from completing an important task deserves greater attention than a minor cosmetic issue.
